en.headline: Chu Hai College finance director remanded over alleged HK$41m theft
en.dek: Ray Yip Kam-chun appeared in Tuen Mun Court on Wednesday facing a theft charge; his wife and an engineering contractor were also denied bail on money-laundering counts.
body: The finance director of Hong Kong Chu Hai College was remanded in custody on Wednesday after appearing in Tuen Mun Court on a charge of theft involving an alleged HK$41 million over roughly three years.

Ray Yip Kam-chun, 49, is accused of stealing from the private college in Tuen Mun between 23 December 2022 and 7 January this year. His wife, Ng Ka-man, 49, and businessman Ho Chung-ling, 50, face a total of 15 counts of money laundering. Prosecutors allege they handled HK$84.7 million and HK$57.9 million respectively through personal and company accounts.

Acting Principal Magistrate Daniel Tang Siu-hung refused bail for all three and adjourned the case to 4 November. The defendants reserved the right to renew bail applications on 20 August and may also apply to the High Court. Yip was first arrested in May after the college president reported unusual transfers totalling about HK$770,000 to his personal account.

zh.headline: 珠海學院財務總監涉盜竊4100萬 還押候訊
zh.dek: 葉錦真周三在屯門裁判法院提堂，被控盜竊罪；妻子及一名工程商亦因清洗黑錢罪名不准保釋。
body: 香港珠海學院財務總監葉錦真（49歲）周三在屯門裁判法院提堂，被控一項盜竊罪，涉在約三年間盜取學院約4100萬元，還押候訊。
控罪指葉於2022年12月23日至今年1月7日期間，在屯門的私立學院盜竊。其妻吳嘉敏（49歲）及商人何鍾凌（50歲）則被控合共15項清洗黑錢罪，分別涉嫌處理約8470萬元及5790萬元。
暫委主任裁判官鄧紹雄拒絕三人保釋申請，案件押後至11月4日再訊。被告保留8月20日再申請保釋的權利，亦可向高等法院申請。葉早前於5月被捕，源於校長向警方報告有約77萬元不尋常轉帳至其個人帳戶。
